body:
Fixes #337

## Summary

The only red run on `008ec1c`, JS CI/CD [39827151731](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/39827151731), was a false positive. It also hid a release that never shipped. I swept every run on that commit for more false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors (logs in [`dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338)), compared the pipeline with the [js](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template), [rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) and [python](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) pipeline templates and with hive-mind's [`CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md), and fixed each defect wherever it occurs.

FP = red without a real defect, FN = green while something is wrong, W = warning.

| # | Kind | Defect | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | FP | `run-with-budget-warning.sh` killed a command up to 1 s early: bash's `SECONDS` counts second *boundaries*, so `-ge budget` fired after `budget - 1 + ε` s. This failed the macOS unit tests and skipped the release of #334. | `-gt` deadlines. Also ports the JS template's hardened wrapper, with `BUDGET_VERBOSE` tracing (off by default). | `js/tests/run-with-budget-warning.js` (deterministic, starts just before a second boundary), `experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs` |
| D2 | FN, W | Rust lint passed with clippy and rustdoc warnings | `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, `check-cargo-warnings.sh`. Warnings fixed. | the CI lint job itself |
| D3 | FP/FN | The changeset check counted every changeset on disk, including the unreleased one from #334 | Count only the files the PR adds (JS changesets and Rust fragments) | `js/tests/validate-changeset.js` |
| D5 | W | `EBADENGINE` for `@opentui/core` (needs Node ≥ 26.4) | Node 26 in every `setup-node` | install logs |
| D6 | W, FN | `allowScripts` named `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.15` while the lockfile has `1.1.0`, so the install script was skipped | Pin refreshed; `strict-allow-scripts` turns future drift into an error | install logs |
| D7 | W, FN | AI SDK `generateObject` deprecation; the warning tests mocked `console.warn`, which AI SDK 7 no longer uses, so they could not fail | `generateText` + `Output.object`; warnings captured through `AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS`, with a self-check | `js/tests/ai-sdk-warnings.ts` |
| D8 | FP annotation | `##[error] No Trusted Publishing config` on a green Rust release | The OIDC step runs only when `vars.CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING == 'true'`; a notice explains the token fallback | — |
| D9 | W | lychee `No files found` for `./**/*.html` | Directory input with `--extensions md,html` | links run log |
| D10 | FN | Instant Release could publish without lint or tests | `needs` + `success` checks on lint, test, verbose-integration and package-install | `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` "release gating" |
| D11 | FN | A first-attempt instant release ended green without publishing when main moved | Only a rerun (`GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT > 1`) counts as finishing an earlier attempt (`scripts/release-rerun.mjs`) | `js/tests/ci-scripts.js` |
| D12 | FN | The gate passed timed-out PR jobs (GitHub reports `timeout-minutes` as *cancelled*) and every result except `failure`; 8 of 10 workflows had no gate | Any unsuccessful result fails. A cancellation passes only if a newer commit replaced the run (`git ls-remote refs/pull/<n>/head`) **and** the job's `cancel-in-progress` evaluates to true (`scripts/job-cancel-policy.mjs`). Gates added to every workflow. `PIPELINE_STATUS_VERBOSE=1` traces each decision. | `js/tests/check-pipeline-status.js` (16 cases), `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` |
| D13 | FN | A Rust release whose crate was missing counted as done; an unreachable crates.io read as "not published" | `scripts/rust-release-state.mjs`: release when the tag, the GitHub release or the crate is missing; 404 = not published; anything else fails with "state unknown" | `js/tests/ci-scripts.js` |
| D14 | FN | The Rust tag was created before the push retry, so it could point at a commit that never reached main | Tag after the push | `js/tests/rust-version-and-commit.js` (races a real concurrent push) |
| D15 | FP | The JS release failed whenever another merge landed during the run | `scripts/push-with-rebase-retry.mjs`: 3 attempts with `git pull --rebase` | `js/tests/ci-scripts.js` |
| D16 | FN | Model tests ran Groq models without `GROQ_API_KEY` | Fail with the secret's name; warn for Kilo (anonymous access works) | — |
| — | true positive | Dependency Freshness on this PR (run 39840971910): 22 AI SDK packages released patches | Refreshed in `package-lock.json` and `bun.lock`; `ip-address` 10.7.4 for GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5 | `scripts/check-npm-freshness.mjs`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile` |

D4 (#334's release never shipped) is a consequence of D1. With D1 fixed, the next push to main releases the pending changeset.

Full analysis, each defect with its evidence, the timeline, every requirement with its status, the options considered, and the components surveyed: [`dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338).

## How to reproduce D1

```bash
git show d274daa^:scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh > /tmp/old-budget.sh
node experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs /tmp/old-budget.sh
# BUG: a command shorter than its budget was terminated (1.4 s command, 2 s budget, killed after 1.40 s)
node experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs
# OK: the command finished inside its budget and was not terminated
cd js && bun test tests/run-with-budget-warning.js
```

## Upstream reports (pipeline templates)

- `SECONDS` early kill: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#252, link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#213, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#116
- Gate treats `cancel-in-progress: ${{ … }}` as unknown and fails superseded PR runs: link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#214
- Gate `needs` parser drops jobs after comments, and a fork's `main` excuses cancellations: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#253
- A fork's branch head excuses cancellations: link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#117
- Related reports that already existed: link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#200, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#106, link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#248

Each report includes a reproduction (the gate reports use `experiments/issue-337/template-gate-*.sh`, which take a template clone as their argument), a workaround and a suggested fix.

## Needs a maintainer

- **crates.io trusted publishing:** a crates.io owner of `link-assistant-agent` must add this repository and `rust.yml` as a trusted publisher, then set the repository variable `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true`. Until then releases publish with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, without the `##[error]` annotation.

## Remaining, out of scope or blocked upstream

See [`open-findings.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/blob/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338/open-findings.md):
- `npm warn deprecated` for `glob@9.3.5` and `node-domexception`: transitive, and the latest upstream releases still depend on them.
- `sprintf-js` moderate advisory: no patched version exists.
- The Ubuntu 26 migration notice: emitted by GitHub.
- `engines.bun` accuracy.

## Verification

- `cd js && npm run check` passes, and `npm test` gives 994 pass / 0 fail.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 (with shellcheck 0.11.0) is clean.
- `zizmor` reports 0 medium/high findings.
- `CHANGESET_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` passes.
- `check-npm-freshness.mjs` passes.
- A changeset (`js/.changeset/ci-false-positives.md`) and a Rust changelog fragment are included.
- CI on `35dfed3`: all 8 workflows pass (JS, Rust, Security, Workflows, Dependency Freshness, Free Model Drift, Model Catalogue, Broken Link Checker).
- In the superseded JS run on `97678b5` ([39845396119](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/39845396119)), the new push cancelled `Check for Changesets` and `Pipeline Status` passed. A timed-out job on an unchanged head fails instead (`js/tests/check-pipeline-status.js`).
- Two failures this PR caused itself in CI were fixed before merge. `bun.lock` was not refreshed together with `package-lock.json` (run 39843280180). A coverage test did not handle CRLF checkouts on Windows (run 39843280202). The logs are in `dev/log/…/ci-logs/pr-*`.
title: fix(ci): remove CI/CD false positives, false negatives and warnings (#337)

body:
Fixes #318.

## Problem

In [the failing release run](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/36386196804), Changesets reported `@link-assistant/agent@0.26.6` published at 06:25:40Z. The seven registry checks ended at 06:27:41Z, 120 seconds later; npm exposed the version six seconds afterward. The job failed before creating the GitHub release.

## Changes

- Poll npm's exact `versions` entry with exponential backoff for five minutes (13 checks), succeeding as soon as the version appears. Record when the publish command succeeded even if verification later times out.
- On a release rerun, sync the checkout to current `main`. If its package version is already on npm, complete a missing tag, GitHub release, or release-note formatting without republishing. A late tag points to the version bump commit.
- Add an always-running release summary that distinguishes npm publication with incomplete post-steps from a version that was not published. Cover both automatic and manual release jobs.
- Create the missing [js-v0.26.6 GitHub release](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/releases/tag/js-v0.26.6) with the pipeline's formatted changelog notes. Its tag points to the 0.26.6 version commit.
- Match the exact npm badge footer before treating release notes as formatted; a misleading URL cannot skip formatting.
- Preserve the confirmed npm publication state if the GitHub release lookup fails, so the summary reports incomplete post-steps correctly.
- Normalize workflow line endings in the wiring test so Windows checkout uses the same assertions.
- Extend the pending patch changeset on `main` so the repository keeps its one changeset per PR rule.

## Reproduction and verification

- Before the fix, the polling test failed: `Received: 120000`, `Expected: >= 300000` milliseconds. The fake registry returns 404 for 20 seconds and then exposes the exact version; the helper succeeds on the fourth check.
- A mocked dry run starts with the version already on npm and no GitHub release, then records tag/release creation and changelog formatting in order, with no publish call. Tests also cover an existing release whose notes still need formatting and a misleading badge URL. The latter test failed before the fix. Workflow wiring checks run against both LF and CRLF text, reproducing the Windows CI failure before normalization.
- A new regression confirms npm publication remains recorded when GitHub release lookup fails; it failed before the fix and passes afterward. The workflow wiring test passes with both LF and CRLF input, addressing the Windows CI failure in [run 36610180845](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/36610180845).
- After merging current `main` locally: `bun run test` passed (808 passed, 4 existing todos, 0 failed); the focused release tests (43 passed), `npm run check`, changeset validation, Docker actionlint, and `npm audit --audit-level=high --package-lock-only` passed. The audit found 0 high and 0 critical vulnerabilities.

<!-- hive-mind:changes:start -->
### Changes
- 10 file(s) modified
- 507 line(s) added
- 12 line(s) removed
- Files:
  - `.github/workflows/js.yml`
  - `js/.changeset/dependency-refresh.md`
  - `js/tests/ci-scripts.js`
  - `scripts/create-github-release.mjs`
  - `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`
  - `scripts/js-release-summary.mjs`
  - `scripts/publish-retry.mjs`
  - `scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs`
  - `scripts/recover-js-release.mjs`
  - `scripts/release-badge.mjs`
<!-- hive-mind:changes:end -->

body:
Fixes #335

## Summary

This ports the reliability fixes that upstream [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) made after our fork point (`0068cb305f`, 2025-11-19, up to `d93568f334`) to the tools, session loop, provider layer and MCP client we already have. **No tools were added.** Each fix applies to code we already have, and each has a regression test.

Upstream moved its code twice since the fork (to Effect services, then from `packages/opencode` to `packages/core`), so no upstream commit could be cherry-picked. I listed all 900 upstream `fix` commits that touch tools, session, provider or MCP code (`docs/case-studies/issue-335/data/`), triaged each one as PORT, ALREADY-HAVE or N/A (`analysis/A–D`), and re-implemented the PORT items in JS. Where a defect also exists in the Rust port, it is fixed in Rust too.

Full case study, including the requirements, timeline, method, online research, libraries considered and verification: [`docs/case-studies/issue-335/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-335-cc63abda9307/docs/case-studies/issue-335).

## What changed

### Edit and write (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parallel edits of one file lost updates | #4388, #23483 | Per-file lock (`FileTime.withLock`) for `edit` and `write` |
| Loose fuzzy match could replace unrelated code; empty `oldString` overwrote a file | #30932 | Stricter thresholds, size guard, explicit error |
| CRLF / mixed endings / UTF-8 BOM not preserved | #9443, #53166, #23797 | Endings and BOM kept; untouched lines never rewritten |
| `replaceAll` interpreted `$&`, `$1` | — | Literal replacement |
| False "modified since read" (clock comparison, `dir/./a` vs `dir/a`) | #17835, #20367 | `{mtime, size}` stamp, canonical path keys |
| `edit` right after `write` failed; empty tool output | `66f9bdab32` | `write` records a read; short confirmations |

### Read, grep, glob, ls (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `glob`/`ls` hung after 100 results (rg blocked on a full pipe) | #10833 | Stream cancelled and rg killed; abort passed through |
| `grep` dropped all matches when one path was unreadable (rg exit 2) | #8612 | Matches kept, plus a note |
| `grep` deadlock on large stderr, no cancel, hidden files skipped | #39238, #7501 | Pipes drained together, abort + 30 s timeout, `--hidden` without `.git` |
| `read` relative to the worktree root, unbounded output, whole file read for the binary check, `\r` leaked | `6cf2c3e3db`, #14009, #51011 | Session directory, 50 KB cap, 4 KB sample, CRLF split |
| macOS screenshot names (U+202F, curly quotes) "not found" | #45807, #50953 | Unique entry matched after canonicalizing |

### Bash and web tools (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bash` ran `/bin/sh` (dash), so bash syntax failed | #3494, #5205 | `$SHELL` if usable, otherwise bash (zsh on macOS) |
| Long output kept the start and dropped the end, where errors are; UTF-8 split (Rust panic) | #22660, #39403 | Tail kept on character boundaries |
| `echo x > file` passed an `echo*` allow rule in read-only/plan mode | #6737 | Write redirects checked as a separate `>` command |
| Rust `bash` deadlocked on full stderr and lost output on timeout | (found here) | Concurrent pipes, partial output, signal reported |
| Web tools: timeout did not cover the body; 5 MB limit checked only after reading it all; Cloudflare 403; Exa key ignored | #21378, #33259, #10328, #16362 | `AbortSignal.timeout`, bounded streaming reader, one honest retry, shared Exa client |
| `Tool.define` stacked wrappers on each init; `task` leaked its subscription | #16952, #9992 | Copy before wrap; `try/finally` |

### Session loop, provider transforms, MCP (JS only; Rust has none of these yet)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context overflow (400 "prompt is too long", 413, `context_length_exceeded`) ended the session | #6480, #14707 | `ContextOverflowError` → compact and continue; a second overflow stops with a clear error |
| Finish `stop` after tool calls ended the loop before the results were sent back | #14973, #26178 | Loop continues while the last step has completed tool calls |
| Retryable 5xx stream errors, plain-text rate limits, Vertex exhaustion, OpenAI item 404, `ZlibError` not retried | #12768, #10590, #24063, #19104 | Classified as retryable; delays capped at 2³¹−1 ms |
| `retry-after` beyond the retry timeout: `process()` returned `undefined` and the loop started another step | (found here) | Normal final-error path, turn stops; retry-only errors added to the message error union (saving them threw a `ZodError`) |
| Lone surrogates, empty Anthropic/Bedrock blocks, empty user messages, foreign signatures/reasoning → 400 | #25934, #4811, `021e42c0bb1`, #21370 | Sanitized per target model |
| Shallow-spread cache options, wrong Bedrock cache point, Moonshot schema errors | #10323, #11664, #18959, #24730, #11984 | `mergeDeep`, `cachePoint: { type: 'default' }`, schema fixes |
| Interrupted tools lost their start time; raw string tool input broke Gemini; tool events without `tool-input-start` dropped | #27254, #21709 | `interrupted` marker, `{ value }` wrapping, `ensureToolCall` |
| Reasoning tokens charged twice; Anthropic thinking budget branch never ran | #21047, (found here) | Charged once; `model.npm` passed |
| MCP: no connect or `tools/list` timeout, endless pagination, sequential listing, leaked failed clients, silent removal on bad URL, no-tools servers failed, results without `content` dropped, timed-out calls kept running, `_` in server names broke per-tool timeouts, connect timeout was `NaN`, grandchildren left on dispose | #6760, #19200, #31442, #13229, #25019, #31595, #31271, #7879, #32244, #15516 | All fixed; see §6.3 of the case study |
| `cancel()` rejected queued callers with `undefined` | `6c9b2c37a5` | `AbortError` |

## Review follow-up: compatibility, memory, Rust parity

Answer to the review comment ("not break anything previously working … configuration for breaking changes … memory leaks … parity between JavaScript and Rust"). Details: §11 of the case study and the audits in `experiments/issue-335/audit/`.

**Backward compatibility.** The JSON input format, event types and envelope are unchanged; stored sessions still load. Every change a script or model could notice has a switch that restores the previous behaviour, as a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var (JS `src/config/config.ts`, Rust `src/compat.rs`):

| Change | Restore previous behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| bash runs `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh` | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a path) |
| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation; read past EOF is an error | `--legacy-tool-output` |
| edit refuses loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on an existing file | `--legacy-edit-matching` |
| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories | `--glob-follow-symlinks` |
| grep searches hidden files and stops after 30 s | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0` |
| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0` |
| context overflow is reported as `ContextOverflowError` | `--legacy-error-names` (non-retryable `APIError`, as before) |
| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens | `--legacy-token-usage` |
| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop | `--legacy-loop-exit` |
| MCP connect is bounded (30 s) | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0` or per-server `connect_timeout` |

MCP `timeout` keeps its old meaning (tools listing); connect got its own `connect_timeout` so that a short listing timeout no longer cuts a slow connect. `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every switch in both states and checks the env wiring in a child process; the Rust switches are tested through `ToolContext::with_settings`.

**Memory and resource leaks fixed (JS):** unbounded SSE usage map; the usage tee branch that stopped reading and made the tee buffer the rest of the stream; bash output and abort-listener retention; grep buffering all rg output; FileTime stamps after a session is deleted; continuous/single-shot mode waiting forever for `session.idle` when a prompt failed early; retried 5xx/429 bodies not cancelled; retry `sleep` abort listener; `withTimeout` timer on rejection; `Instance.dispose()` leaving the cache entry; pending permission asks of a cancelled turn. Each has a regression test. Two items were left on purpose (client disconnect does not cancel a turn; the per-request provider timeout signal) — reasons in §11.2.

**Rust parity.** `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `read`, `edit`, `bash`, `todo`, `batch`, `webfetch`, `websearch` now match the JS tools (output, errors, limits; edit diffs checked against output of the JS code), with the same compatibility switches plus `--read-only` / `--disable-tools`. Latent Rust bugs fixed: non-ASCII panic in `permission.rs`, prefix match in `Filesystem::contains`, panic on an empty id. Not done, with reasons: FileTime and the per-file lock (each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session), permission checks in tools (the Rust CLI never runs tools for a model), and the absent LLM/session/provider/MCP layers (pre-existing). Divergences are listed in `experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md`.

**CI checks that also failed on `main`** (fixed here, no manual step; §11.4 of the case study):

- **Security:** `body-parser` 2.3.0 (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, high), bumped to 2.4.0 in both lockfiles.
- **Free Model Drift:** Kilo withdrew `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, the default model and first compaction model in JS and Rust. The defaults are now `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (cascade `(kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free kilo/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free same)`). For backward compatibility `kilo/nemotron-3-super-free` (and the bare short name) stays accepted as a deprecated alias that runs on Ultra and logs a warning naming the replacement; the drift script skips aliases and checks that their targets are built-ins.
- **Model Catalogue:** `check-default-models.mjs` reported the same withdrawn default; fixed by the new default. The alias warning lives in `kilo-deprecation.ts` so `kilo.ts` stays dependency-free (this workflow runs without installing packages).
- **Dependency Freshness:** all direct npm dependencies bumped to latest (AI SDK and `@ai-sdk/*`, MCP SDK, opentui 0.8, `glob` 14, `minimatch` 11, `hono`, `command-stream` 2.6, …; no source changes needed). `solid-js` unpinned (opentui#689 is closed) and the obsolete `seroval` override dropped. `lino-arguments` stays on 0.3.x and is pinned: 0.4.0 makes the agent exit at startup when the host has both `http_proxy` and `HTTP_PROXY` (reported upstream: link-foundation/lino-arguments#50). Rust: `globset`, `ignore`, `similar` and `uuid` updated to their latest patch releases for `cargo outdated`.

**Crash in git worktrees and submodules (found while checking the dependency refresh).** `Project.fromDirectory` wrote its id cache to `.git/opencode` without awaiting or handling the write. In a worktree or submodule `.git` is a file, so the write rejected with `ENOTDIR` and the `unhandledRejection` handler exited the CLI with code 1, on every run. The id is now cached in the common git dir (as upstream does) and a failed write is only logged. Reproduction: `bun experiments/issue-335/project-worktree.ts <worktree dir>`; regression test `js/tests/project-worktree.ts` fails before the fix and passes after.

## Deliberate deviations from upstream

- **No new tools** (requirement of the issue): `apply_patch`, `lsp`, `question`, `skill`, `plan-*` and `code-mode` were not added. The unregistered `patch` and `multiedit` stay unregistered.
- **`write` keeps "no restrictions"**: upstream requires a prior read; the fork removed that on purpose (`db682c8`).
- **Image formats**: upstream stopped sending SVG/BMP/TIFF/ICO/AVIF as images (#21114). The fork supports them on a maintainer's request (`86f24ac`), so that change was not ported.
- After an overflow compaction, upstream replays the user message; here the existing flow (summary plus a synthetic "Continue if you have next steps") is kept.

Known remaining limitation: when a model overflows, the compaction model cascade does not move on to the next model; the overflow is reported instead.

## How to reproduce (example: lost parallel edits)

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/main origin/main && cp -r experiments/issue-335 /tmp/main/experiments/
ln -s "$PWD/js/node_modules" /tmp/main/js/node_modules
(cd /tmp/main && bun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts)
# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=15 rejected=1
bun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts
# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=0 rejected=0
```

Other reproductions are in `experiments/issue-335/{edit-write,read-search,bash-web}/`.

## Tests

- New: `js/tests/edit-write-reliability.ts`, `read-search-reliability-{read,search}.ts`, `bash-web-reliability.ts`, `session-reliability.ts`, `provider-transform-reliability.ts`, `mcp-reliability.ts` (with a stdio MCP fixture server), `compat-flags.ts` (every compatibility switch in both states, env wiring, leak regressions), `project-worktree.ts`; Kilo alias tests in `free-model-catalog.ts` / `model-drift.ts`; Rust `rust/tests/compat.rs` and `rust/tests/tool_{edit,write,read,grep,glob,bash,webfetch,websearch,codesearch}.rs` (plus the parity tests).
- `cd js && bun test --timeout 30000 ./tests/*.js ./tests/*.ts`: 1150 pass, 4 todo, 0 fail before the review follow-up; the full suite runs in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows for every push.
- Review follow-up, locally: 10 focused JS files (compat, session, MCP, models, CLI options, AI SDK, project worktree, snapshot) 187 pass, 0 fail; `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `check:file-size` clean; `bun scripts/check-model-drift.mjs` and `node scripts/check-npm-freshness.mjs` exit 0; `npm audit --audit-level=high` clean.
- `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test`: clean, 563 pass.

Release notes: `js/.changeset/sync-opencode-stability-fixes.md` (the JS pipeline accepts one changeset per PR, so it also covers the default model, the worktree crash and the dependency refresh); `rust/changelog.d/20261022_220339_sync_opencode_stability_fixes.md`, `20261103_002356_tool_js_parity_and_compat_switches.md`, `20261103_120000_kilo_default_model_withdrawn.md`, `20261103_130000_crate_patch_updates.md`.
title: fix: sync reliability fixes for existing tools, session loop, providers and MCP from upstream OpenCode (#335)

Fixes #301.

## Problem

JS CI/CD run [33551125228](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/33551125228)
went red on `main` with

```
Error updating npm: $ is not a function
```

after all six checks had passed. Auditing that run end to end surfaced a second
class of problem: several steps could not have failed the pipeline even when
they were broken, and the release gates could not tell a timeout from a pass.

## Root cause of the reported failure

`use-m` resolves a package with `createRequire(...).resolve`, so the `require`
condition wins and `command-stream@>=0.19.0` is loaded through its **CommonJS**
entry point. Node.js 23+ adds a synthetic `'module.exports'` named export to
CommonJS namespaces, which `use-m` does not recognise as metadata, so it stops
unwrapping the callable default:

```console
$ npx --yes node@24 --input-type=module -e "…const loaded = await use('command-stream')…"
{"node":"v24.20.0","keys":["default","module.exports"],"dollar":"undefined","defaultDollar":"function"}

$ npx --yes node@20 …
{"node":"v20.20.2","keys":["AnsiUtils",…,"$","default"],"dollar":"function","defaultDollar":"function"}
```

`const { $ } = await use('command-stream')` therefore yields `undefined`, and the
first tagged template throws. `scripts/use-module.mjs` normalizes the namespace on
every Node version; the eight release scripts now go through it.

## What changed

**False negatives — CI could not fail**

- A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as *cancelled*, not
  failed, and every release gate reads `needs.<job>.result == 'success'`, so a
  timed-out check silently skipped the release and left the run green. Both
  pipelines gained a `pipeline-status` job backed by `scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`.
- `bun add "$TARBALL" | tee install.log` reported `tee`'s status (no `pipefail`);
  `npx prettier --write ".changeset/*.md" || true` and
  `cat ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json || echo "not found"` swallowed real failures.
- `npm install -g npm@latest` was unverified, and unpinned: the runner silently
  jumped 11.16.0 → 12.0.2 mid-pipeline. It is now pinned to the tested major and
  the OIDC minimum (11.5.1) is asserted.
- Nothing scanned dependencies (53 npm advisories, 12 high; RUSTSEC-2026-0258 in
  `Cargo.lock`), nothing linted the workflows, nothing checked links.
- Long steps had no deadline of their own, so they ran into the job timeout and
  produced the silent cancellation above; `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`
  now warns at 70% and kills the process group at 100%.

**Errors and warnings**

- `npm warn allow-scripts` for `@parcel/watcher` and `tree-sitter-bash` — native
  builds were being skipped.
- 53 advisories → 36, 0 high/0 critical (unused `@actions/*` packages and the
  vulnerable `undici` they pulled in are gone; `h2` bumped past RUSTSEC-2026-0258).
- 8× `LF will be replaced by CRLF` on windows-latest, and the AI SDK
  *"System messages in the prompt or messages fields can be a security risk"*
  warning — both fixed, the latter with a test that pins the warning and its absence.
- 23 actionlint/shellcheck findings and 12 zizmor findings, including a
  `${{ github.base_ref }}` template injection and 11 mutable action tags.

**New workflows** — `workflows.yml` (actionlint + shellcheck + zizmor),
`security.yml` (CodeQL, dependency review, `npm audit`, `cargo audit`, weekly),
`links.yml` (lychee + Wayback fallback). All seven workflow files now follow
principle 10 of [CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md):
per-job `check-…` groups that cancel off `main`, and a single non-cancellable
`main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main` group shared by every `main` writer.

## Tests

New suites: `js/tests/use-module.js`, `setup-npm.js`, `check-pipeline-status.js`,
`run-with-budget-warning.js`, `check-web-archive.js`; `workflow-policy.js` extended
to accept per-job concurrency and to reject a cancellable writer, so the
concurrency policy cannot regress.

```
762 pass, 4 todo, 0 fail, 1545 expect() calls, 66 files
npm run check            → exit 0
actionlint 1.7.7         → exit 0
zizmor 1.30.0            → No findings to report (min-confidence medium)
```

## One action left for a repository admin

`actions/dependency-review-action` failed on every pull request with
*"Dependency review is not supported on this repository"* — the dependency graph
is disabled for `link-assistant/agent` (`GET /dependency-graph/compare/…` → 403,
`/dependency-graph/sbom` → 404), which no workflow change can turn on. The job now
probes that API and skips the review with a `::warning::` on 403/404 instead of
failing the run, and still fails on any other status and on real advisories.
Enabling **Settings → Code security → Dependency graph** restores the full check
with no further code change; `npm audit` and `cargo audit` cover the lockfiles
meanwhile. That warning annotation is the only one left in the pipeline, together
with the upstream-only `npm warn deprecated node-domexception@1.0.0`
([fetch-blob#175](https://github.com/node-fetch/fetch-blob/issues/175); even
`fetch-blob@4.0.0` still depends on it, so it cannot be fixed downstream).

## Reported upstream

| Upstream | Report |
| --- | --- |
| `link-foundation/use-m` | [comment on #72](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/72#issuecomment-5505355202) — Node 24.20.0 reproduction, downstream incident, and the `'module.exports'` metadata-key fix |
| `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | [#151](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/151) — the identical `const { $ } = await use('command-stream')` pattern in `setup-npm.mjs` and seven sibling scripts, on `node-version: '24.x'` runners |
| `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | [#145](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/145) — workflow-scoped `main-write` concurrency group does not serialize `main` writers from another workflow |

## Evidence and analysis

Every claim above is reproducible from
[`dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-301-ef35bbf03fb8/dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302):
the raw run logs, the [timeline](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/timeline.md), each
[requirement](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/requirements.md) of the issue with its
status, the [root cause](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/root-causes.md) of every
finding, the [options considered](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/solution-plans.md)
including the file-by-file comparison against both pipeline templates, the
[components surveyed](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/existing-components.md), and the
[findings left open](dev/log/issues/301/pulls/302/open-findings.md) with reasoning.

Debug tracing added by this PR is off by default: set `CI_SCRIPTS_DEBUG=1` to have
`scripts/use-module.mjs` print the resolved module shape, which is what makes an
interop regression like this one readable from a CI log alone.

## Note on the changeset

`js/.changeset` already carried an unreleased entry and
`scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` allows exactly one changeset per pull request, so
this change is described inside that file rather than added as a second one.
title: fix(ci): audit both pipelines for false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors

body:
Convert existing token publishing for crates-io: link-assistant-agent in rust.yml. Review the build, versioning, triggers and job dependencies before merging. Then re-run setup --migrate to attach the trusted publishers to the caller workflow and verify an OIDC release before cleaning up legacy secrets.

## Fallback: trusted publishing first, token second
The auth step has `continue-on-error: true`, and the publish step reads `${{ steps.prm_auth.outputs.token || secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN }}`. Publishing uses the short-lived OIDC token whenever crates.io trusts this workflow, and falls back to the token secret otherwise (for example before the publisher is registered, or if OIDC is unavailable). The token secrets are **kept** as that fallback.

## Changes
- `.github/workflows/rust.yml`: both release jobs (`auto-release`, `manual-release`) get `id-token: write`. Each one also gets a `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action` step, pinned to `c6f97d42…` (tag `v1.0.5`), that runs right before `Publish to crates.io` under the same `if:` condition as that step.
- `scripts/publish-to-crates.mjs`: the doc comment now says where `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` comes from. The logic is unchanged.
- `rust/changelog.d/20261013_145108_trusted_publishing.md`: patch fragment that describes the OIDC publishing and the token fallback.

## Verification
- `actionlint` 1.7.7, using the same Docker image as the `Workflows` CI job: no findings.
- `zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml --min-confidence medium .github/workflows/`: no findings. This matches `main`.
- `bun test ./js/tests/workflow-policy.js`: 15 pass, 0 fail.
- The OIDC path can only be tested end to end by a real release, after the trusted publisher is registered on crates.io for `link-assistant/agent` / `rust.yml`. Until then the token fallback is used, so release behaviour does not change.
title: Migrate registry publishing to OIDC

body:
## Summary

Fixes #334. The agent now supports every AI provider that [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) supports, the OpenAI-compatible services and local API of [gpt4free](https://github.com/xtekky/gpt4free), and live model discovery, so new models work without an agent release or a docs edit.

### Providers (OpenCode parity)

OpenCode's providers are the [models.dev](https://models.dev) catalogue plus provider-specific code in its loaders and auth plugins. Both parts are covered here.

- **Every models.dev provider loads** (`js/src/provider/env-template.ts`, `provider.ts`). Base URLs with `${ENV}` templates (Cloudflare, Databricks, Snowflake Cortex, Vertex, Neon and others) are filled from the environment the same way OpenCode fills them. Per-model endpoints are honoured. Variables that only name an account, region or project are never sent as an API key.
- **Custom loaders ported from OpenCode** (`js/src/provider/parity-loaders.ts`):
  - Amazon Bedrock, including Mantle, with cross-region prefixes;
  - Google Vertex: ADC through `google-auth-library` and the regional `aiplatform.googleapis.com` hosts;
  - Cloudflare AI Gateway and Workers AI;
  - Snowflake Cortex and SAP AI Core;
  - Venice and AIHubMix, which fall back to their OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- **Subscription logins ported to `agent auth login`** (`js/src/auth/provider-logins.ts`, `azure-login.ts`):
  - xAI (SuperGrok) device login, with token refresh;
  - Poe browser login (PKCE) and DigitalOcean browser login;
  - GitLab (gitlab.com and self-managed);
  - Azure Microsoft Entra ID through the Azure CLI. It uses a bearer token per audience, `cognitiveservices` or the Foundry `ai.azure.com`.

  These join the existing Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Google, Qwen and Kilo logins.
- **`prompt_cache_key`** is sent to the openai-compatible providers OpenCode enables it for (`transform.ts`).

**Not ported, on purpose:**
- **OpenCode's _Console_ login.** It signs in to OpenCode's own organisation control plane with OpenCode's client identity, so another client cannot use it. OpenCode Zen models still work with `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
- **Listing Azure deployments through the Azure management API.** The agent uses the data-plane deployments listing instead, which accepts both API keys and Entra ID tokens.

Both are documented in `docs/providers.md` and `docs/model-discovery.md`.

### gpt4free

Added in `js/src/provider/extra-providers.ts` and documented in `docs/gpt4free.md`:

- **`gpt4free`** (`g4f`): the local Interference API. `G4F_PROVIDER` routes requests to one of gpt4free's providers via `/api/{provider}`.
- **`g4f-space`**: the hosted gateway.
- **`pollinations`**.
- **Key-based OpenAI-compatible services from gpt4free's provider list**: `airforce`, `aibadgr`, `api-route`, `cheaperinference` and `theb`.
- **Local servers**: `ollama`, `vllm`, `llamacpp` and `omniroute`. `lmstudio` (from models.dev) is made keyless.

The rest of gpt4free's providers fall into two groups. Most are services models.dev already lists, such as OpenRouter, Groq, DeepInfra, Together, Cerebras and Nvidia. The others scrape web apps or need a browser session, so they are only reachable through the gpt4free API.

Keyless providers are **explicit-only**: they never become the default and never answer a short model name, so a stray local server cannot take over a run. Routers and local servers pass unknown model IDs through unchanged.

### Dynamic model info (ideas from hive-mind)

Added `js/src/provider/model-discovery.ts` and the `agent models --discover / --refresh / --free` options:

- **Live listings.** Each provider's own token-free listing endpoint (`/models`, Anthropic, Google, Cohere, Azure deployments, Vercel AI Gateway, Kilo) adds models released since the last models.dev update. models.dev only supplies their metadata.
- **Hive-mind rules.** Endpoints that spend tokens are refused before any request. Results are cached for at least one hour. The cache key covers the provider, the URL and a scrypt fingerprint of the credential.
- **Unknown `--model`.** The agent refreshes models.dev, then checks the live listing, then passes the ID through for routers. Otherwise it fails clearly instead of switching to another model.
- **Opt-out.** `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_MODEL_DISCOVERY=off` disables live listings.

### Docs

- **New:** `docs/providers.md`, `docs/gpt4free.md` and `docs/model-discovery.md`.
  - `docs/providers.md` covers credentials, logins and parity notes. It also has a generated table of all models.dev providers: run `bun scripts/generate-provider-docs.mjs`, or add `--check` to verify it.
- **Refreshed:** `MODELS.md` and `FREE_MODELS.md` now list current models, and the usage examples put free models (Kilo, gpt4free, Pollinations, local servers) before paid ones.
- **Updated:** `README.md` and `js/README.md` link to the new pages.

### CodeQL findings

All inline CodeQL comments on this PR are fixed:

- **Discovery cache key:** the credential is now fingerprinted with scrypt.
- **Vertex host check:** the hostname is anchored with a regex.
- **DigitalOcean login page:** it uses a literal token path.
- **OAuth and Azure experiments:** the RESULT lines report only whether each credential equals its expected mock value, never the value itself.
- **Provider docs generator:** table cells escape backslashes as well as pipes.

### CI fixes needed for this PR (they also failed on `main`)

- **Release left consumed changesets behind.** Changesets 3 formats the changelog through the package manager it detects. Because of `js/bun.lock` that is `bun x prettier`, and the release job had no Bun. The 0.26.15 release log shows `spawn bun ENOENT`: `changeset version` had already bumped the version but crashed before deleting the changeset files. command-stream's `$` does not throw on a non-zero exit, so the release still committed.

  As a result, `js/.changeset/recoverable-tool-error-not-fatal.md` (already released in 0.26.15) stayed on `main` and failed this PR's one-changeset check. The fix:
  - set up Bun in the release job;
  - make `scripts/changeset-version.mjs` fail on a non-zero exit, and verify that no changeset is left (`scripts/changeset-files.mjs`);
  - remove the stale changeset.

  Repro: `experiments/issue-334/changeset-version-without-bun.sh`.
- **Dependency Freshness:** all unpinned npm dependencies are updated to their latest releases (AI SDK providers, `ai` 7, `google-auth-library` 11, eslint 10 and others), and tokio is updated to 1.54.1. Rust changelog fragment included.
- **Security (npm and cargo audit):** new advisories against transitive dependencies. `launch-editor` (pulled in by `@changesets/cli`) is updated to 2.14.2 (high severity, GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw). Rust `rustls-webpki` is updated to 0.103.16 (RUSTSEC-2026-0382) and `webpki-root-certs` to 1.0.10 (RUSTSEC-2026-0383).
- **Packed bash-tool check (`experiments/issue-322/verify-bash-parser.mjs`):** Bun 1.4.4 no longer prints the `incorrect peer dependency` warning, so the script failed on CI's latest Bun but passed on 1.4.3. I reproduced this with both versions. `npm ls`, which still reports the invalid peer, is now the check; the warning text is verified only when Bun prints it.
- **Workflows (zizmor):** `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`'s `master` branch moved, so the `# master` pin comment no longer matched. The action is now pinned to the current `master` commit.

The Rust crate has no LLM provider integration, so provider work there is out of scope; its only change is the tokio update.

### Cross-platform test fixes

The end-to-end probe tests failed on macOS and Windows:
- **Temp directory check.** The probe scripts required `XDG_DATA_HOME` to contain `tmp`, but `os.tmpdir()` is `/var/folders/.../T` on macOS and `...\Temp` on Windows. They now check that the directory is inside `os.tmpdir()`. Reproduced on Linux with `TMPDIR=$HOME/fakeT`: 2 failures before the fix, none after.
- **CRLF output.** On Windows `agent models` ends lines with CRLF, so the models helper now splits on `\r?\n`.
- **Fake Azure CLI.** The Azure test also writes an `az.cmd` fake for Windows.
- **Diagnostics.** The tests now include the probe's stderr when it fails.

### How to reproduce / tests

- **`js/tests/provider-parity.ts`** (34 tests): env templates, model discovery (billable-endpoint guard, TTL, cache key, parsers), extra providers, every parity loader, `prompt_cache_key`, the provider registry end to end, and `agent models --discover/--refresh/--free` against local mock servers.
- **`js/tests/provider-logins.ts`** (24 tests): the xAI, Poe, DigitalOcean and GitLab logins against mocked authorization servers, and stored logins reaching the provider registry.
- **`js/tests/azure-login.ts`** (13 tests): Azure CLI tokens, the Entra ID fetch, the plugin, deployment discovery, and an end-to-end run with a fake `az`.
- **`js/tests/ci-scripts.js` and `js/tests/workflow-policy.js`:** the changeset-consumed check, and Bun being set up before the release step. Both fail without the fix.
- **Scripts:** `experiments/issue-334/` has the scripts used to probe the registry, the logins, Azure and the CLI.

Locally, `npm test` reports 949 pass and 0 fail, and `npm run check` is clean. Rust `cargo test`, `fmt` and CI-style `clippy` pass. zizmor (config and confidence as in CI) reports no findings.
title: feat: support all OpenCode AI providers and gpt4free, with live model discovery

Agent 0.26.11 selected the withdrawn `opencode/minimax-m2.5-free` model and included other withdrawn Zen IDs in its compaction defaults. Add a catalogue guard so every shipped default and compaction entry must be served by its provider or have non-deprecated models.dev metadata.

Fixes #328.

- Merge current main, preserving PR #329's served Kilo defaults, exact gateway aliases, Zen `FreeTierError` handling, refreshed dependencies, and JavaScript 0.26.12 / Rust 0.10.3 releases.
- Check the default, single compaction model, and expanded cascade directly from shipped constants. Resolve `same`, deduplicate entries, and translate Kilo aliases to their exact gateway IDs. Environment overrides cannot hide stale defaults.
- Run offline regression and Rust parity tests plus the live check on relevant pull requests, main changes, daily, and manual dispatch. Catalogue failures produce diagnostics; another valid source may establish availability. No inference calls or credentials are needed.
- Preserve MiniMax shared-provider withdrawal coverage, dated catalogue evidence, and a replay experiment. Refresh the packed parser experiment to the current runtime while preserving OpenTUI's supported peer pins.

### Reproduction and tests

The original defaults fail the evidence replay with four withdrawn IDs. The catalogue regression suite originally had three failures; preserving main's new Kilo defaults reproduced four additional failures until the checker handled exact gateway IDs. The replay now reports zero unavailable current defaults.

```bash
bun experiments/issue-328/reproduce.ts
bun test ./js/tests/default-model-catalogue.ts
bun scripts/check-default-models.mjs
cd js && npm test && npm run check
cd ../rust && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 cargo test --all-features --locked -j 1
```

The 15 catalogue tests cover shipped values, Rust parity, deduplication and `same`, exact Kilo IDs and withdrawals, provider identity, deprecated/missing metadata, endpoint fallback, and malformed responses. The live checker accepts all current shipped defaults. Catalogue availability does not establish authentication, pricing, or successful inference; main's Kilo defaults preserve the separate Zen client-restriction fix.

### Dependency freshness follow-up

The prior-head [freshness run](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/38216083935) failed with 28 outdated npm packages and a closed parser-pin issue (downloaded log lines 182–212), plus serde_json 1.0.151 → 1.0.154, tokio 1.53.1 → 1.53.2, and uuid 1.26.1 → 1.28.0 (lines 674–679). The same commands failed locally before the updates and now pass. The completed dependency refresh is also present in the merged main branch.

Solid 1.9.12 and web-tree-sitter 0.25.10 remain exact peers required by OpenTUI 0.6.1, with active upstream trackers [#689](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/689) and [#1550](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/1550). The freshness gate remains unchanged. Packed Agent tests pass with both parser runtimes and reproduce the newer runtime's upstream peer conflict.

### Validation

- Merged JavaScript unit suite: **869 passed, 4 existing TODOs, 0 failures**.
- Both dependency freshness commands, frozen Bun install, ESLint, Prettier, size limits, actionlint, live catalogue check, and evidence replay passed.
- Packed parser tests: **12 passed per runtime**, for 0.25.10 and 0.27.1. Eleven shell-parity cases passed under both Node and Bun after the command-stream upgrade.
- Rust all-features suite: **436 passed, 0 failures** across 83 targets, including doctests; built sequentially with debug info disabled for the container memory budget.
- Rust formatting, Clippy, workflow security validation, release-fragment validation, and verbose HTTP logging integration passed. Clippy retains existing warnings; the npm high/critical audit passes with four moderate upstream advisories.
- All eight workflows passed for commit `4585619`: 26 successful PR checks, including CodeQL, and five expected release-job skips. Both [`npm outdated` and `cargo outdated`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/38225612101) passed on that exact commit; [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/38225597973) and [Rust](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/38225597966) pipelines also passed. No freshness or security gate was weakened.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #332. A tool call that fails and is recovered from (`read` on a missing file, a bad edit anchor, a non-zero `bash` exit) is no longer emitted as a top-level `{"type":"error"}` event. That type is reserved for failures that end the turn or the session, which is how Hive Mind treats it.

### Root cause

`js/src/cli/event-handler.js` (`outputBusEvent`) emitted **two** events for every failed tool part: the `tool_use` event, which already carries `part.state.status: "error"` and the error text, and a duplicate top-level `type: "error"` event (written to stderr). In the incident log, Hive Mind saw that duplicate and logged *"Agent exited 0 after an error event; the error event in its output still fails the run"*, and the run failed with `Agent reported error: Error: File not found: …/e.g`. The model had in fact read the tool result, finished the turn with `reason: "stop"`, and the agent had exited 0.

The Claude `stream-json` adapter depended on the duplicate: it turned the `error` event back into the terminal `tool_result` with `status: "error"`. Because the source event was an `error`, that `tool_result` went to **stderr** instead of stdout.

### Changes

- `js/src/cli/event-handler.js`: a failed tool call is reported only on its `tool_use` event. Top-level `error` events now come only from `session.error` and the CLI-level failure paths.
- `js/src/json-standard/index.ts`: the Claude adapter builds the error `tool_result` directly from the `tool_use` snapshot (`errorText(state.error, 'Tool execution failed')`). It now goes to stdout like every other tool result. The tool-specific branch of the `error` case was removed.
- `docs/stdin-mode.md` → *Error Events*: documents the contract. `error` means the turn or session failed, and a failed tool call shows up only as `tool_use` with `state.status: "error"` (OpenCode) or `tool_result` with `status: "error"` (Claude). `js/README.md` links to it.
- Case study: `docs/case-studies/issue-332/README.md`. Changeset: patch.

Of the options listed in the issue, I chose "report only on `tool_use`" over a new `tool_error` type or a `recoverable: true` flag. The information is already on the `tool_use` event, and a separate event would be one more type for consumers to classify.

### How to reproduce / tests

- **`js/tests/recoverable-tool-error.ts`** (new, end to end): runs the real CLI against a local OpenAI-compatible mock. The first turn calls `read` on a missing file and the follow-up turn answers with text. For both `--json-standard opencode` and `claude` the test asserts that:
  - the model received `File not found`,
  - the failure appears on the tool's own event (Claude: on stdout, not stderr),
  - the model continued and the exit code is 0,
  - **the stream contains no `error` event**.

  Before the fix, both tests failed and showed exactly the event from the incident (`{"type":"error",…,"message":"Error: File not found: …/e.g"}`).
- **`js/tests/event-handler.js`**: the two #289 tests that asserted the old duplicate event were replaced. A failed tool part, with or without error detail, now yields only `tool_use` and does not call `onError`. A `session.error` is still a fatal `error` with a readable `message`. The Claude error `tool_result` goes to stdout, renders object errors, and falls back to `Tool execution failed`.

Locally, before the fix: 5 of the new or changed tests fail. After the fix: `npm test` reports 874 pass, 0 fail, and `npm run check` (eslint, prettier, file size) is clean.

### Note for consumers

OpenCode-format consumers that used the duplicate `error` event to detect tool failures should read `part.state.status === "error"` on `tool_use` instead. Hive Mind's side is tracked in link-assistant/hive-mind#3213.

### Housekeeping

- Removed `js/.changeset/served-free-models.md`. Its content was already released in full in 0.26.13 (and partly in 0.26.12), but the file stayed on `main`, so it failed the one-changeset-per-PR check and would have been released a third time. This follows the same precedent as `d5ea9bd`.
- Removed the auto-generated `.gitkeep` placeholder.
title: fix: stop emitting recoverable tool failures as fatal error events
